pr_title: Change matrix component to use matrix-nio instead of matrix_client
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This PR introduces a new dependency, [matrix-nio](https://github.com/poljar/matrix-nio), as a replacement for the obsolete `matrix_client`.
- Allows for the use of `asyncio` operations to greatly speed up operations involving network I/O.
- Will allow for use of E2EE, and other important features of Matrix that have become common in the last few years.
- Because the developers of the old dependency, [matrix-python-sdk](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-python-sdk/tree/887f5d55e16518a0a2bef4f2d6bff6ecf48d18c1), specifically recommend the use of `matrix-nio` as "both more featureful and more actively maintained".

Furthermore, this PR aimed to validate the dependency upgrade by introducing new unit tests (was previously NOT tested) and python type hinting. Currently, I've achieved **_97%_** code coverage of the component code.


## Type of change
<!--
  What type of change does your PR introduce to Home Assistant?
  NOTE: Please, check only 1! box!
  If your PR requires multiple boxes to be checked, you'll most likely need to
  split it into multiple PRs. This makes things easier and faster to code review.
-->

- [x] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New integration (thank you!)
- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [x] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information
<!--
  Details are important, and help maintainers processing your PR.
  Please be sure to fill out additional details, if applicable.
-->
THIS SHOULD NOT BE A BREAKING CHANGE.

Every effort was taken to maintain (and test!) all previous functionality, with the exception of exact code logic (and resulting logging statements) used to achieve it.

I have deliberately *not* done any refactoring of existing code except as to take advantage of newer python syntax or to support best testing practices. If such cleanup is desired, I can perform it in this PR, or in a separate PR.

I have also deliberately not implemented Config Flow, in order to keep PR size down. Its implementation, along with other matrix-specific features, are in my future plans.

I am happy to explain any apparent functionality difference, or fix it if it is actually incorrectly replicating existing behavior.

Though I have checked multiple boxes under `Type of change`, this was done solely in light of how the `matrix` component currently does not have any unit tests, and I thought it would be prudent/appropriate to include such tests while making such a reaching change.

If, before/during review it is requested to split the dependency upgrade and addition of unit tests into separate PRs, I am happy to do so.

@elefon After poking around a bit at the code, I think I'm actually going to hold off on implementing the use of `m.notice` until later (or ofc, you/anyone else would be welcome to take it on).

My reasoning is that there's a bit of a misnomer in the existing design: the `ATTR_FORMAT` entry in the schema, which currently accepts `"text"` or `"html"`, would be the most natural place to add a new option, `notice`.
The problem though, is that an HTML matrix message isn't actually different from any other `m.text` message, besides the requirement of the formatted body. It'd be just as reasonable to allow for HTML `m.notice` messages.

Unfortunately, I can't think of a "clean" way to separate these separate concepts of "formatting" and "matrix `m.room.message` type" without adding a whole new field in the config entry... which seems overkill and a bit too far away from the spirit from making a 1:1 function translation for the scope of this PR.

Ideally, I'd actually want to even introduce a breaking change where an entirely new parameter could be specified that has the exact type, among `m.text`, `m.notice`, and `m.emote` (which is another omission from the original component that I feel should be allowable, but I don't see a reasonable way to include without the same messy problem).

This'd be the first step to allowing HASS to fully construct an entire Matrix Event, rather than simply only messages.

I'm happy to say at least that overriding this behavior and just making *all* of your HASS messages `m.notice` is still really easy with a 1-line code change in this PR... which is better than the alternative? I'm open to opinions/other ideas that keep the changes minimal, and ofc I'm very excited at the prospect of doing this the right way once this is all merged :)

> too far away from the spirit from making a 1:1 function translation for the scope of this PR As I said, I'm fine with that. I hope your PR gets approved in the near future. > separate concepts of "formatting" and "matrix m.room.message type" without adding a whole new field in the config entry So adding `ATTR_TYPE = "type"` is a bigger deal? From my quick glance at the code it looked as if it could just be added as optional attribute. But in that case it makes even more sense to make a new PR. I thought that one could just (in short): * add it in `__init__.py`, ``` ATTR_TYPE = "type" MESSAGE_TYPES = [MSG_TYPE_TEXT, MSG_TYPE_NOTICE, MSG_TYPE_EMOTE] DEFAULT_MESSAGE_TYPE = MSG_TYPE_TEXT ``` * import it and then: ``` if data is not None and data.get(ATTR_TYPE) == [...] ``` * and send like ``` # Example of notification as HTML action: service: notify.matrix_notify_notice data: message: >-

issue_context.title: matrix-client is unmaintained
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Logging in with Home Assistant on a Dendrite instance fails, because the `matrix-client` library expects `home_server` in the 
 dict of the `m.login.password` api endpoint, but `home_server` [has been deprecated](https://spec.matrix.org/unstable/client-server-api/#post_matrixclientv3login) and was removed from Dendrite.

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/setup.py", line 256, in _async_setup_component
    result = await task
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 58, in run
    result = self.fn(*self.args, **self.kwargs)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/matrix/__init__.py", line 98, in setup
    bot = MatrixBot(
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/matrix/__init__.py", line 179, in __init__
    self._client = self._login()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/matrix/__init__.py", line 322, in _login
    client = self._login_by_password()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/matrix/__init__.py", line 351, in _login_by_password
    _client.login_with_password(self._mx_id, self._password)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/matrix_client/client.py", line 257, in login_with_password
    return self.login(username, password, limit, sync=True)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/matrix_client/client.py", line 282, in login
    self.hs = response["home_server"]
KeyError: 'home_server'
```

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.3.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Matrix

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/matrix/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

It still works with Synapse, so using a matrix.org account or any other account hosted on a Synapse instance will work, until they remove the deprecated value from the login response.

review_comments:
Hi @PaarthShah , really great work you have done so far. I came to the HA repo to start a PR introducing the  message type [m.notice](https://spec.matrix.org/v1.3/client-server-api/#mroommessage-msgtypes) to the existing matrix component, when I saw yours.

Could you imagine introducing a new optional attribute `ATTR_TYPE = "type"` which can hold a value `notice` and passes it on to the send function, just like the `ATTR_FORMAT` does?

The motivation for this comes from having a chatbot to interact with HA. When I write some kind of command, I want to get an immediate response as acknowledgement but don't want all my other matrix clients to fire a notification sound when this bot response arrives.

Hi @efelon! Appreciate you taking the time to look at this!

Totally agreed that implementing the use of `m.notice` would be a good and important addition. I'd be happy to take a crack at it (and fix that last test failure 🙃) in the upcoming week!

My only _slight_ concern is that I didn't originally want to do extra feature work in this initial PR since I didn't want to confound the 1:1 translation of the old code to the new code... But honestly adding something this small and fundamental isn't going to delay its review/merging any further, so I'm in

In truth, my very original motivation for this PR was that I wanted HASS to be able to participate in/initiate entire Threads/respond to reactions! Heck, we even have live location sharing in Element/synapse now...

My long-term goal is to let this integration be fully capable of sending/responding to any particular matrix event

> But honestly adding something this small and fundamental isn't going to delay its review/merging any further,

Exactly what I thought. Since it is only a few lines in the end, I decided to leave a comment and not to dive into the overhead of creating a PR only for it.

> , so I'm in

🤩

> My long-term goal is to let this integration be fully capable of sending/responding to any particular matrix event

That is one kind of a vision, with a lot of work behind. I will keep an eye on your work and wish you all the best for it. Keep in mind that the matrix spec. is still very fluid. Especially in terms of new features like threads or live location sharing. IMHO the next important thing is having the E2EE handling (cross signing, verification requests, ...) somehow manageable in HA (in the config flow I guess).
